name: RS-25 (SSME)
tagline: Reusable, hydrogen-fuelled, and still flying on SLS
description: The RS-25 was the engine the Space Shuttle Main Engine program spent a decade perfecting: a staged-combustion cycle on LOX and LH2 that could throttle, restart, and be refurbished for the next flight. Over 135 Shuttle missions from April 1981 it accumulated a near-perfect operational record. The engines were recovered, inspected, and reflown — an ambition that no earlier rocket engine had achieved at this power level. After the Shuttle retired, the inventory was requalified and repurposed for NASA's Space Launch System, where RS-25s now power SLS's core stage.
best_known_for: Reusable staged-combustion engine — 135 Shuttle flights, now flies on SLS
